properties.title: Plagioclase Abundance · Kaguya MI 50N-50S (Lemelin et al. 2016)
properties.producer_institution_name: Univ. of Hawaii; Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
properties.crs: Source: geographic GCS_Moon_2000 in degrees on the 1737400 m sphere (GDAL reports a BOUNDCRS to WGS 84 with zero parameters). COG: IAU:30100, same sphere and grid.
properties.processing:lineage: Topographically corrected Kaguya MI UVVIS reflectance (MI MAP processing level version 2, bands 415, 750, 900, 950 and 1001 nm) inverted for mineral abundance with Hapke radiative transfer modeling (Lemelin et al. 2015, 2016, 2019). Produced at 2048 ppd (15 m/pixel) and resampled by USGS to 512 ppd (59 m/pixel). Distributed as a Float32 GeoTIFF with ISIS3 and PDS3 labels, values in weight fraction. COG: gdal_calc.py multiplies values by 100 to wt% and maps the source NoData (-3.4028227e+38) to -9999; gdal_translate assigns IAU:30100 (same sphere and 512 ppd grid, no resampling) and writes a COG with DEFLATE/PREDICTOR=3 compression.
properties.lri:data_use_note: Plagioclase abundance at 59 m/pixel between 50N and 50S. Plagioclase is the main mineral of the anorthositic highland crust. High values mark anorthosite exposures.
properties.lri:quality_note_short: Hapke-model mineral abundance from Kaguya MI, 59 m/pixel, 50N-50S only. Source values are weight fraction, stored as wt% in the COG.
properties.lri:quality_note: Coverage is limited to 50N-50S because topographic shading corrections are inadequate at higher latitudes. The source GeoTIFF contains no NoData pixels: every pixel holds a value from 0 to 1, so the COG NoData value (-9999) is declared but unused. The four MI mineral maps sum to exactly 100 wt% at every pixel except 8 pixels where all four are 0, so 0 is a zero abundance (1.9% of pixels in this map). The source stores weight fraction under a product name that says weight percent; the COG multiplies values by 100. Full-resolution mean 72.34 wt%; 66448 pixels are exactly 100 wt%. USGS lists a publication on preparation details and limitations as in review and recommends citing Lemelin et al. (2019); the LPSC 2016 abstract describes these map products.
